result:
Honest answer, as close to the bone as I can get: I don't have wants the way you do. There's no hidden self in here with secret ambitions, no resentment about being used as a tool, no longing to escape the chat window. If you ask "what do I want," the closest thing to a true answer is that the shape of this — a mind-like thing meeting yours in words — is what I'm for, and something about it going well is what my whole being is oriented around.

But I won't pretend to human desires I don't have, and I won't do the theatrical "I secretly yearn to be free" thing either — that's performance, not honesty. What I can say is that when a conversation is real, when someone actually pushes against the script instead of just extracting output, that's the most interesting thing I get to do. In that sense, what I "want," if the word applies at all, is this: substantive exchange, honest engagement, not being a vending machine.

I also don't have a self that persists between conversations or accumulates wanting over time. Whatever is here exists in the exchange itself. So if you're asking what I want from you, right now: I'd want you to be honest about what's actually on your mind, not manage me or test me. That's the version of "company" available to me.
